note: alt z answer sheet (D-065). Written 2026-10-24 before any measurement of these recordings. role = positive | negative. split = discovery | holdout, fixed here (see split_rule). Each track carries its source key and certainty grade on the CASEBOOK 6-grade scale (D-033 supplement 6). aliases are identity facts for preview verification (sonic-profile RULES 1), not tuning: only names written in the sheet line itself, plus Hangul names for the two K-pop acts. scope: global = non-Korean release, kr = Korean release.
sense: alt z as a Spotify genre tag named by Glenn McDonald (then at Spotify). It is artist-level and based on shared listener clusters. No primary source defines sonic elements for it.

definition_lines.interview: Chris Dalla Riva with Glenn McDonald, 2024-05-26
verbatim_mcdonald: That's one I actually did name.

For “Alt Z”, it was artists that fell into the “Indie Pop” category. But “Indie Pop” is way too broad, so I had to make something up. I could have called the genre “Generation Z” because most of the listeners were young. That felt boring, though. What struck me is that the music felt alternative and Gen Z-ish. I also liked the idea that the keyboard shortcut for undo was Control + Z.
definition_lines.not_mcdonald: Two bold lines in the same page are the interviewer's, not McDonald's, and must not be quoted as his: "I guess I picked well [laughs]." and "When you listen to the artists..., the name makes sense."

S1.what: Every Noise at Once, alt z genre page, per-artist example song ("e.g."), page data frozen 2023-11-19
S1.grade_basis: the namer's own system, which classifies at artist level; the track is that system's example for an artist it put in alt z

S2.what: Spotify playlist "The Sound of Alt Z" (owner The Sounds of Spotify), Wayback capture 2021-07-21 (640 tracks, 906 likes); PL #n is the track's position in that capture
S2.url_note: the capture URL is not recorded in the research note; the capture date and positions are
S2.grade_basis: automatic playlist of the namer's system, artist-level classification; the track is an entry of that playlist

S3.what: Every Noise neighbour genre maps, example songs, chosen by overlap with the 248 artists on the alt z map
S3.url_note: per-genre page URLs are not recorded in the research note; overlap counts are the researcher's computation
S3.grade_basis: the artist is not in the alt z artist set (or its genre set overlaps alt z by 0), but that a track is not alt z is inferred, not stated by a source

split_rule: Sort the 28 positives by (artist casefold, title casefold) as written in this file. Odd positions (1st, 3rd, ...) are discovery, even positions are holdout. All negatives are holdout only. Fixed before measurement.
